name: Cleena

attributes.attribute: a Munster fairy queen and goddess of beauty

text: Cleena is the anglicized spelling of Clidna, an Irish goddess famed for great beauty. The goddess belongs to Munster lore and is linked with County Cork. Tradition tells how she drowned in Glandore harbour. The wave that took her is remembered as Tonn Chliodhna, the wave of Clidna. Munster tradition also honours Clidna as a fairy queen. MacKillop treats Cleena as a cross-reference. Readers should turn to Clidna for the main article on this goddess.

okr.objective: Cleena is the Anglicization of Clidna, the Munster goddess associated with Co. Cork.
key_results: Cleena is the anglicized form of the name Clidna.
Clidna is a goddess of great beauty linked with Co. Cork and drowned in Glandore harbour.
The drowning wave is remembered as Tonn Chliodhna, and Munster tradition knows her as a fairy queen.
The main article appears under the name Clidna.
